summary: GitHub concurrency groups are per repository, so ADR-0097 serializes all FS-GG publishers with a bakery lock over the public Actions job list: the oldest in-progress participant job proceeds, the job's end is the release, a 7 h lease ignores ghosts and waiters fail closed. The first design identified participants by a gate step in the job step list; review measured that the REST jobs API returns empty step lists for many in-progress and completed jobs, so participation is now decided only by job-level fields (a [org-publication-writer] marker in the job name, status, started_at, runner_name) and the ticket is the server-side started_at. Waiting is queueing: lock-bearing writer jobs raise their timeout, and the workflow-timeouts ceiling, by exactly the bounded wait. Limits: registered producer repositories adopt through their own PRs, FS.GG.Coordination is exempt (its Actions allow-list admits no FS-GG action), the live-main equality guard is unchanged, and no publication has yet run under the lock.
title: The org publication writer lock recognises participants by job name, because the Actions step list is unreliable
